claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start by asking: **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

**Are you and Alex currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Are you responsible for Alex?** By this I mean, do you look after Alex and pay towards the costs of raising them (such as food, clothes, housing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after Alex and pay for everything they need - food, clothes, school things, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** (This is relevant for children aged 16-19, but I want to make sure I have all the information about Alex's situation.) Also, **is there any special circumstance I should know about, such as Alex being in hospital, in care, or living with someone else temporarily?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - a few months. They've been there getting treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. I understand Alex has been in hospital for a few months receiving treatment.

Before I can complete my assessment, I need to read the specific guidance about children in hospital to ensure I give you accurate information about your eligibility.

Let me check the relevant rules now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I have a clearer understanding of the rules. I need to ask you an important follow-up question about Alex's hospital stay:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex while they are in hospital?** This could include things like buying them clothes, toys, treats, personal items, or other expenses for them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that. I mean, it's been difficult with them being in hospital for so long. I haven't really thought about whether what I'm doing counts as "regularly spending" or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a difficult situation and you have a lot on your mind. Let me ask this in a more straightforward way:

**Have you been buying things for Alex since they've been in hospital - for example, have you bought them any clothes, toys, books, treats, toiletries, or other personal items during these few months they've been there?** Even occasional purchases would be relevant here.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I'm not certain. With everything going on, I haven't really kept track of whether I've been spending on them or not. It's all been quite overwhelming.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is clearly a very difficult and overwhelming time for you and your family.

Let me ask one more question to help clarify the situation: **Has Alex been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks, or has it been less than 12 weeks? Or have they had any breaks where they came home for a period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been more than 12 weeks now - they've been there continuously for a few months without coming home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I understand this has been a very difficult time for you and your family.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me explain the situation:

According to the UK Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into hospital for more than 12 weeks, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit after that 12-week period. However, there is an important exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on them while they're in hospital.

Since Alex has been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks, and you've indicated that you're not certain whether you've been regularly spending money on them during this time, I cannot definitively determine whether you meet the exception that would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit.

This means your eligibility is **indeterminate** based on the information available. You would need to:
- Review whether you have been making regular purchases for Alex (clothes, toys, treats, toiletries, etc.)
- Contact HMRC directly to discuss your specific circumstances

They will be able to assess whether any spending you have done qualifies as "regularly spending money" on Alex, which would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit despite the hospital stay exceeding 12 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your situation. They'll be able to look at your specific circumstances and help you determine whether you qualify for the exception that allows Child Benefit to continue when a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks.

I hope Alex recovers well, and I wish you and your family all the best during this challenging time.
